source_text:
Testamentum ad cives
∆ιαθήκη πρὸς τοὺς πολίτας.
31 προτείνουσι δ' οὖν ὅμως διαθήκην πρὸς τοὺς πολίτας διατεταγμένην, καθ'
ἣν μὴ ἀναφέρειν εἰκόνας ἐπ' ἐκκλησίας ἢ ἐν κοιμητηρίοις παρεγγυᾷ.
thought_title: The testament's first command against images
orientation: Epiphanius is issuing a binding testament to the citizens, and this section states its first command: not to bring images into churches or cemeteries.
pass_a_gloss: They put forward, then, nevertheless, a testament to the citizens, an ordered testament, according to which he urges not to bring images up onto churches or in cemeteries.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'testament' for διαθήκη, preserving the binding legal force of the term.
The glossary requires 'images' for εἰκόνας, avoiding terms that imply idolatry or later icon terminology.
The glossary requires 'cemeteries' for κοιμητηρίοις, avoiding euphemistic or overly literal renderings.
The verb ἀναφέρω has the sense of carrying or bringing something up to a place; 'bring up' preserves the directional force.
παρεγγυάω means to give a command or instruction; 'urges' captures the exhortative force without overstating it as a legal decree.

pass_b_english: They put forward, then, a testament to the citizens, in which it urges that images not be brought into churches or into the cemeteries.

problems.quote: They put forward, then, a testament directed to the citizens, in which he urges
problems.source_quote: προτείνουσι δ' οὖν ὅμως διαθήκην πρὸς τοὺς πολίτας διατεταγμένην, καθ' ἣν μὴ ἀναφέρειν εἰκόνας ἐπ' ἐκκλησίας ἢ ἐν κοιμητηρίοις παρεγγυᾷ
problems.why: Subject switches from 'they' to 'he' with no antecedent; source uses third-person throughout.
problems.fix: They put forward, then, a testament directed to the citizens, in which it urges that images not be brought into churches or into the cemeteries.
problems.ruling: παρεγγυᾷ is singular third person; 'they put forward' then 'he urges' lacks antecedent, misleading reader on agency.

problems.why: Intro says 'citizens' are recipients; text shifts between 'to' and 'directed to'

variants.text: a testament directed to the citizens

problems.why: Antecedent of 'it' unclear—testament? Epiphanius? shifts from 'they'

problems.quote: They put forward, then, a testament directed to the citizens, in which it urges
problems.why: 'They' is unexplained; reader cannot identify who is putting forward the testament.

edits.old: They put forward, then, a testament directed to the citizens, in which it urges
edits.new: Epiphanius puts forward, then, a testament to the citizens, in which he urges

fixed: Changed 'They' to 'Epiphanius' to identify the speaker, and 'directed to' to 'to' for consistent phrasing with the intro.
Changed 'it' to 'he' to refer to Epiphanius.

problems.quote: Epiphanius puts forward, then, a testament
problems.why: Third-person narration intrudes without warning; rest is first-person speech.
problems.fix: Frame consistently as Epiphanius's own words or add editorial markers.

problems.quote: Epiphanius puts forward, then, a testament to the citizens
problems.why: Reader cannot tell if this is Epiphanius speaking of himself or an editor narrating about him.
problems.fix: Mark editorial narration distinctly from the text of the testament itself.

edits.old: Epiphanius puts forward, then, a testament to the citizens, in which he urges
edits.new: They put forward, then, a testament to the citizens, in which it urges

fixed: The source has no explicit subject for 'put forward'; the English supplied 'Epiphanius' and 'he', which created the speaker confusion. Restoring the impersonal 'They put forward... in which it urges' matches the source's third-person frame without intruding into the testament's first-person voice.

last_rejected.source_quote: καθ' ἣν μὴ ἀναφέρειν εἰκόνας ἐπ' ἐκκλησίας ἢ ἐν κοιμητηρίοις παρεγγυᾷ
last_rejected.why: Subject 'it' obscures agent; source has active verb with author as subject.
last_rejected.fix: in which he urges that images not be brought into churches or into the cemeteries.
last_rejected.ruling: παρεγγυᾷ active verb with 'testament' as antecedent of καθ' ἥν; 'it' correctly refers to the testament, not obscuring agency.
